note: Corpus callosum malformations are frequently reported in GTF3C3 cohorts alongside cerebellar anomalies, but appear partially penetrant across published case series.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 12 individuals from 7 families with biallelic GTF3C3 variants, individuals presented with intellectual disability, motor impairments, seizures, and variable cerebellar and corpus callosum malformations.

source.title: Biallelic variants in GTF3C3 result in an autosomal recessive disorder with intellectual disability
source.quote: The cohort presented with intellectual disability, variable nonfamilial facial features, motor impairments, seizures, and cerebellar/corpus callosum malformations.

evidence.text: Evaluation of 4 patients with biallelic GTF3C3 variants identified variable brain malformations including cerebellar atrophy, frontal hypoplasia, and corpus callosum aplasia/hypoplasia, demonstrating phenotypic variability.
